briefdescription.para: NRH-01: Primary region all backends down → cross-region fallback succeeds; returned code is OK (not connection-closing).
NRH-02: All regions fully down → ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE, not connection-closing (transport stays open, caller decides retry).
NRH-03: After kFailoverThreshold consecutive failures LB switches from PRIMARY to STANDBY — no connection-closing error emitted.
NRH-04: After kRecoveryThreshold consecutive successes on STANDBY, LB recovers back to PRIMARY — deterministic round-trip.
NRH-05: ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE is not connection-closing — routing errors belong to cluster-layer, not transport-layer.
NRH-06: QUORUM_DEGRADED is not connection-closing and not a rate-limit transient — it is a cluster health signal only.
NRH-07: When all backends are degraded/down, router returns exactly ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE — no undefined code, no infinite loop.
NRH-08: AdaptiveCircuitBreaker opens after failure_threshold consecutive failures; subsequent requests are fast-rejected (shouldAllow() returns false).
Phase 3 — Routing and Topology Hardening focused tests (NRH-01..NRH-08).

detaileddescription.para:
Covers the two Q4 2026 open items from src/network/ROADMAP.md § Phase 3:
Expand routing correctness checks under changing health/latency/topology signals.
Harden load-balancing state transitions and recovery under churn.

Also covers the Q4 2026 Planned Feature:
Strengthen distributed routing and failover diagnostics for operator triage.
All tests are deterministic and self-contained — no live sockets, no external dependencies beyond the contract header.

sect2.title: Test Cases

para.heading: NRH-01..NRH-02 — Topology-Aware Routing Under Region Failure

sect2.para: NRH-01 Primary region fully down → router falls back to secondary region; fallback result is not connection-closing (routing rerouted). NRH-02 Cross-region fallback exhausted (all regions down) → ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE returned; not connection-closing.

para.heading: NRH-03..NRH-04 — Load-Balancer State Transitions Under Churn

sect2.para: NRH-03 Load balancer switches from primary to standby after threshold consecutive failures without returning a connection-closing error. NRH-04 Load balancer recovers to primary after standby delivers consecutive successes — state transitions are deterministic.

NRH-05 ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE is not connection-closing — cluster routing errors do not terminate transport connections. NRH-06 QUORUM_DEGRADED is not connection-closing and not rate-limit transient — it is a cluster-level signal only.

para.heading: NRH-07 — All Backends Degraded: Deterministic Fallback

sect2.para: NRH-07 When every tracked backend is degraded, the router returns ROUTING_UNAVAILABLE (not an unexpected error code) and does not loop infinitely.

para.heading: NRH-08 — Circuit Breaker Integration with Routing

sect2.para: NRH-08 After failure_threshold consecutive failures the circuit OPENS; subsequent routing attempts are fast-rejected (no call through).
